clinician.trajectory_summary: A 63-year-old woman with ESRD on hemodialysis for 6 years presented with acute 1-day history of large neck swelling, hoarseness, and progressive dysphagia. She had a known 1-year history of nodular goiter (initially grape-sized on either lobe). On presentation, she had respiratory acidosis due to hypoxia on ABGA. Physical examination revealed a markedly large nodular goiter without lymphadenopathies. Laboratory studies showed normal platelet and coagulation function, and normal thyroid function tests. Ultrasound revealed multiple thyroid nodules and a well-defined mass behind the trachea. Contrast-enhanced CT at 24 hours showed a nonenhancing, enlarged mass behind the trachea compressing both the airway and esophagus, consistent with acute hemorrhage. Due to laryngeal compression, endotracheal intubation was performed with a 6.0 Fr tube. An urgent partial thyroidectomy was performed successfully. Postoperative CT confirmed excision of the left thyroid lobe and hematoma. The patient was extubated on postoperative day 4 and discharged on postoperative day 10. On follow-up, she had complete resolution of compressive symptoms and hoarseness, with normal blood calcium levels and no mass on repeat neck ultrasound at 1 month.
